sentences.text: 1. This appeal has been filed by the appellant - State under Section 378(1)(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code') against the order passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himmatnagar (hereinafter referred to as 'the learned Trial Court') in Criminal State Of Gujarat - Thro' D.T.Trivedi, ... vs Suresh K Shah - Thro' Atulkumar Kantilal ...

on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196393896/
1

Case No. 1069 of 1996 on 11.01.2013, whereby, the learned Trial Court has acquitted the respondents - accused from the offences punishable NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined under Sections 2(1a) and 7(1)(5) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
1.1. The respondents hereinafter referred to as 'the accused' as they stood in the rank and file in the original case, for the sake of convenience, clarity and brevity.

2. The relevant facts leading to filing of the present appeal are as under:
2.1. The complainant - Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi was a notified Food Inspector and on 09.10.1991 at around 13:15 hours, visited the shop of the accused no. 1 and gave his identity as a Food Inspector.

The complainant purchased 450 grams of 'mustard oil' of 'Gopi Brand' from a packed tin and paid Rs.15.30 paisa and after the entire procedure was followed, the 450 grams of mustard oil was placed in equal proportions in three clean and dry glass jars.

The glass jars were sealed and labeled and placed in brown paper and sealed and one sample was sent to the Public Analyst,
Rajkot as per the procedure and the other two samples were sent to the Assistant Commissioner and Local Health Authority, Gandhinagar.

The report of the Public Analyst was received, which showed that the sample did not conform to the standards and provisions laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, and after the permission for filing the complaint was received, the complaint was filed by the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined complainant Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi against the accused no.1 - the vendor, the accused no.2 - the wholesaler and the accused no.3 - the producer of the mustard oil.
2.2.

The learned Trial Court was pleased to take cognizance of the offence and the summons were issued to the accused and the accused Nos. 1 and 2 were duly served with the summons and appeared before the learned Trial Court.

During the trial before the learned Trial Court, the accused no. 3, who was the producer, could not be traced out and the complainant could not produce the new address of the accused no.
3 and non-bailable warrants were issued, but could not be served.

2.3. During the pendency of the trial, the complainant Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi expired on 23.05.1998 and the accused nos. 2 and 3 filed an application at Exh.38 stating that as the complainant has expired, the complaint may be dismissed under the provision of 256 of the Cr.P.C. and they may be acquitted from the offence under the Food Adulteration Act as it is mandatory for the complainant to prove the case.

In support of their say, they have produced the copy of the death certificate of the complainant at Exh.45 and on perusal of the same, it transpires that the complainant Mr.Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi has expired on 23.05.1998.

Considering the above, the learned Trial Court was pleased to dismiss the complaint by the impugned order NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT State Of Gujarat - Thro' D.T.Trivedi, ... vs Suresh K Shah - Thro' Atulkumar Kantilal ... on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196393896/
2 DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined dated 11.01.2013 and was pleased to acquit the accused from the complaint filed against them.

sentences.text: 3. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned order passed by the learned Trial Court, the appellant - State has filed the present appeal mainly stating that the impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the learned Trial Court is contrary to law and evidence on record.
The learned Trial Court has erred in evaluating the documentary evidence on record of the case and without appreciating the evidence in its real perspective, acquitted the accused.

The learned Trial Court ought to have call the in- charge Food Inspector in place of the deceased Food Inspector Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi and on behalf of the department, he could have deposed on the basis of the record available which was not done at the relevant time.

The learned Trial Court has erred in not appreciating that there is no reason for not taking any oral evidence in absence of the complainant, who expired, as the panch witness was available and the Food Inspector was also available, but no oral evidence have been recorded.

The learned Trial Court has passed the impugned order of acquittal without giving any cogent and convincing reasons and the same is illegal, invalid and improper, and therefore, the same requires to be quashed and set aside.

4. Heard learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined State,
learned advocate Mr.J.V.Japee for the respondent no. 1 and learned advocate Mr.D.K.Modi for the respondent no.2.
Perused the impugned order of acquittal and have re-appreciated the entire evidence of the prosecution on record of the case.

5. Learned APP Ms.C.M.Shah for the appellant - State has submitted that the non availability of the original Food Inspector, who had collected the sample, on account of his unfortunate demise,
cannot be a circumstance to defeat the prosecution case so as to allow the accused to escape liability,
particularly when the report of the Public Analyst on record clearly establishes that the sample of the food article was not in conformity with the standards prescribed under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules.

Learned APP further submits that the documentary evidence on record unerringly demonstrates that all mandatory requirements under the Prevention Food Adulteration Act and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules were duly complied with, and therefore, the accused was liable to be convicted and punished in accordance with law.
Learned APP has urged this Court to quash and set aside the impugned order of acquittal and to find the accused guilty for the said offence and impose maximum sentence on the accused.

6. Learned advocate Mr.M.D.Modi for the respondents submits that as per the case of the Food Inspector, the sample was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
08/08/2025 undefined collected on 09.10.1991 and the report of the Public Analyst is dated 11.11.1991 and the sanction to file the case is dated 29.02.1996 and the Food Inspector filed the complaint on 20.04.1996.
For many years, the present respondents were appearing before the State Of Gujarat - Thro' D.T.Trivedi, ... vs Suresh K Shah - Thro' Atulkumar Kantilal ...

on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196393896/
3 learned Trial Court but the respondent no. 3 was not appearing, and hence, the respondent nos. 1 and 2 filed the discharge application at Exh.40 on 29.09.2009, after the lapse of almost 18 years from the date of offence and after 13 years from the date of launching the prosecution.
Subsequently, the application was withdrawn.

Thereafter, the death certificate of the complainant was produced on record and the learned Trial Court was pleased to pass the impugned order, and hence, the present appeal may be dismissed.
6.1.
Learned advocate Mr.M.D.Modi has relied upon the following decisions:

1. State of Gujarat Vs. Ashokkumar Aasandas Kotak and Anr. reported in 2007(2)
FAC 50.
2. State of Gujarat Vs. Bharatkumar Keshavlal Bhatt (Seller) reported in 2010(0)
GLHEL-HC 226132.
[
7. On perusal of the entire record of the case, it appears that in the present case that the original complainant - Food Inspector, Mr.Dilipkumar Trambaklal Trivedi, who had collected the sample,
who was the principal witness to the alleged offence, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined expired during the pendency of the proceedings.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note that the samples were collected on 09.10.1991, whereas the complaint came to be filed only on 20.04.1996, after an unexplained delay of nearly four years and eight months.

While the demise of the Food Inspector who collected the sample would not, by itself, vitiate the prosecution, it was incumbent upon the prosecution to establish its case by leading cogent evidence,
such as examining witnesses, who had been present at the time of collection of the sample.

It is settled law that when the witness was not available due to his sad demise or otherwise, the important right of cross-examination of the witness was not effectively available to the accused and the accused would not have the full opportunity to put up his defence.

In the absence of such evidence, and having regard to the fact that no other material was brought on record to sustain the charge, the learned Trial Court, in the proper exercise of powers under Section 256 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, was justified in dismissing the complaint and recording the acquittal.
8. In view of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the learned Trial Court was completely justified in acquitting the accused of the charges leveled against them.
The order recorded by the learned Trial Court is absolutely just and proper and no illegality or infirmity has been committed by the learned Trial Court.

This Court finds no reason to interfere with NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1691/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 08/08/2025 undefined the impugned judgment and order and the present appeal is devoid of merits and resultantly, the same is dismissed.
9.
The impugned order passed in Criminal Case No.1069 of 1996 by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Himmatnagar on 11.01.2013 is hereby confirmed.
